items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: He was a hell of a trumpet player. And he taught everybody in that area. In fact he taught Illinois Jacquet.

ctx.x: I’m constantly amazed by the family traditions in New Orleans. And we’ll talk maybe later about your children. But was your family, your parents, your siblings, were they as musical as your kids?

No they wasn’t. They, in fact my father now, I didn’t come from New Orleans, I came from a little town they called Crowley, Louisiana. And he had some cousins that played. But my daddy used to get, on a Saturday night sometimes when he had a few little drinks in him, he would pick up accordion and try to keep up with them. But they played guitar and bass, his cousins, our cousins. So they had a band but he would try, but if he didn’t have a few drinks in him he wouldn’t even deal with it at all other than the…
